card.name: Life-threatening after diabetic ketoacidosis
card.fires_on: The word "a" or the hyphen-joined "-threatening" in the phrase "diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening event". It occurs in SGLT2-inhibitor warnings about type 1 diabetes.

modes.label: Article before life-threatening
modes.description: The word "a" right after "diabetic ketoacidosis," where "life-threatening" comes next.
modes.example: significantly increases the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis,<< a>> life-threatening event, beyond the background rate

modes.label: Inside life-threatening
modes.description: The "-threatening" part of "life-threatening" in the same sentence.
modes.example: bexagliflozin tablets significantly increase the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis, a life<<-threatening>> event, beyond background rate. In placebo

card.writes: It seems to push toward words meaning severe or critical, such as "critical" and "严重".
card.plain: It marks the spot in the ketoacidosis warning where the text calls the event life-threatening.
